name: Data path model
bounds: Three brokers, one partition, and at most three leader epochs, with log length 4 (data_clean, data_unclean) or 3 (data_elr).
outside: Record payloads, transactions, remote storage, multiple partitions, and the last-known-ELR half of KIP-966 remain outside the model.
summary: Composes the production high-watermark core with the ISR expansion kernel, the leader-epoch truncation lookup, the controller failover decision, the KIP-966 recovery election and ELR maintenance rule, fetch visibility, and the diskless WAL-durable HWM and offset reservation. It checks that committed records stay durable, that a clean election loses nothing, that an ELR election keeps every record that reached the HWM, and that only an election reported as losing data sets the lost flag.

name: Producer state model
bounds: One producer ID over one- and two-record batches; the basic config covers epochs 0 and 1 with sequences through 6, the wide config epochs through 3 with sequences through 9.
outside: The model enumerates submit sequences rather than concurrent requests, and offsets, snapshots, and transactions remain outside it.
summary: Drives the host's retained-batch bookkeeping around the proved producer_decision kernel and compares every answer with an independent classification by Kafka's rules over a ghost window of the five batches Kafka retains. Any disagreement becomes a counterexample, and witnesses require duplicates of the last, an older, and the oldest retained batch, an out-of-order refusal, and an epoch bump.

name: Replica state model
bounds: One partition with three replicas, a fixed leader, and log ends through 3.
outside: Wall-clock lag, the controller's AlterPartition path, and I/O remain outside the model.
summary: Holds the production ReplicaState and explores every interleaving of leader append, follower fetch, and ISR installation. It requires the high watermark to stay nonnegative, inside the leader's log, and nondecreasing, every ISR member to hold every committed record, follower log ends clamped to the leader's, and the leader in the ISR.

name: Fetch session model
bounds: Topic references over two names and two IDs; the basic config uses four references and the wide config seven.
outside: Session epochs, eviction, and the wire codec remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production KIP-227 forget-then-merge composition over sequences of incremental fetches whose topic references carry a name only, an ID only, or both, so the search covers a rename and a conflicting ID on one partition. It requires that no two cached keys name one logical partition and that every cached entry carries a requested max_bytes.

name: Fetch visibility model
bounds: Partition watermarks kept in Kafka's order with log ends through 4 (basic) and 7 (wide).
outside: Record reads, remote tiers, and the fetch-session cache remain outside the model.
summary: Advances the partition watermarks one at a time and probes every consumer and follower fetch shape at every offset up to one past the log end. Each probe checks the clamp contract (a consumer never reads at or past the high watermark or the delivery watermark, a read-committed consumer stops at min(lso, hw), a follower reads to the log end), that every fetcher is told the partition's high watermark and min(lso, hw), and that neither reported watermark regresses.

name: Leader failover model
bounds: One three-replica partition with assignment [1, 3, 2], brokers dying, reviving, and rejoining the ISR, at min.insync.replicas 1 and 2.

pinned_states.config: offset_recovery (each of 16 published-ELR and witness combinations)

outside: Logs, and so the completeness of an elected replica, are outside this model; data_path_model checks that.
summary: Drives the production controller failover decision and checks each one against Kafka's one-broker rule for a fenced broker and against the rung ladder of PartitionChangeBuilder.electAnyLeader: clean election in assignment order from the target ISR or ELR, offset-aware recovery only with no live ISR and no electable ELR member, the KIP-841 unclean election only when enabled, and Unavailable only when no rung was open. It requires the ISR within the replicas, a non-witness leader inside its ISR, and ELR disjoint from ISR.

name: Reassignment model
bounds: One partition with leader epochs through 10; reassign_basic has replicas 1 to 3 adding 3 and removing 2, reassign_leader_handoff removes the leader, and reassign_wide has five replicas adding two and removing two with the leader removed.
outside: Catch-up is an explicit action rather than a replicated log; the AlterPartitionReassignments planner and controller submission remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production KIP-455 completion step through every interleaving of an adding replica joining the ISR, broker death and revival, and completion ticks. It requires every decision to wait for all adding replicas, a handoff to move leadership to an alive in-ISR target that is not being removed while bumping the epoch by exactly one, and a completion to install exactly the target replica set with the leader inside it.

name: Stretch cluster model
bounds: Three sites with one broker each, replication.factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2, a witness replica in the third site, leader epochs through 6, and at most two sites down or isolated at once.
outside: The controller may decide in every state, including states without a metadata quorum, which over-approximates the reachable set; KRaft itself, logs, and I/O remain outside the model.
summary: Checks KFC-2's witness claim: a witness never leads, an acks=all produce commits whenever at most one site is impaired and the controller has converged, every leader change carries a strictly greater epoch, a site set without a voter majority never commits, and a preferred election keeps the leader in the preferred site when it can. Two RED configs must fail: the pre-witness controller breaks leader_never_witness and min.insync.replicas 1 breaks minority_never_commits.

name: Diskless crash model
bounds: Offsets through two, two appenders, three WAL members with at most one lost, sequencer epochs through two, and every reachable ordering of reservation, fsync, crash, object PUT, index commit, trim, member loss, and sequencer handoff, at depth 15.
outside: WAL members, fsync, PUT, and index commit are counters rather than logs or objects, every reservation stays pending, the trim runs with no safety lag, and the idempotent-producer dedup rebuild is not modeled.
summary: Composes the diskless WAL design's crash windows with the quorum rule and stateless appenders, with three production kernels deciding the steps. It requires the quorum-acknowledged and producer-acknowledged frontiers to survive a minority WAL loss, a sequencer handoff never to lower the quorum-durable frontier, every trim to stay at or below both the committed index frontier and the quorum-durable frontier, and reservations to be gap-free and unique.

name: Client-server failover model
bounds: Three brokers, one producer identity with one batch, logs of at most one batch, a high watermark through 1, at most four send attempts and four metadata refreshes.
outside: The wire client, transactions, and unclean election remain outside the model.
summary: Composes a producer client's failover routing and retry bookkeeping with the production idempotent-producer check over every interleaving of send, retry, replication, high-watermark advance, acknowledgement, leader death, clean election, and metadata refresh. Eleven always properties require that an acknowledged batch is committed and stays durable, that no log holds the batch twice, that a reroute never skips a sequence, that every leader holds the committed prefix, and that the attempt and refresh caps hold.

name: Quorum WAL model
bounds: Three voters, at most two one-record batches, leader epochs 0 through 2, and every ordering of up to eight enabled operations, at depth 9.
outside: The production diskless path where remote voters fetch the leader's tail (record_follower_ack, serve_fetch) is covered by unit tests instead, and allocation, fsync, and crash atomicity below successful filesystem calls remain I/O assumptions.
summary: Drives the in-process three-replica harness over real Log instances: record-batch append, replica sync with byte verification of each replica's whole retained log, acknowledgement and watermark advancement, and byte-agreement recovery, truncation, and repair. It keeps the watermark inside the leader log, preserves every committed prefix, requires a byte-identical quorum at the committed frontier, and checks every acknowledgement against its rule.

name: Classic group model
bounds: The basic config has two members, one instance ID, and a clock through 4; the wide config three members, two instance IDs, and a clock through 5.
outside: Wire decoding, the offsets log, and the actor mailbox remain outside the model.
summary: Wraps the production ClassicGroup and explores every interleaving of dynamic, static, and fenced joins, heartbeats, leaves, rebalance completion, sync, and session-timeout expiry over a logical clock. It requires a coherent static-member index, one live owner per group.instance.id, only current members in the round, an empty member set exactly in the Empty state, and expiry exactly when a member is past its session timeout.

name: Consumer group composition model
bounds: The basic config has two members, two partitions, and epochs through 6; the wide config three members, two partitions, and epochs through 5.
outside: Plain consumer groups deliver at least once, so no-duplicate and no-gap delivery are deliberately not checked; __consumer_offsets persistence and the classic protocol are out of scope.
summary: Reuses the reconciliation model's driving of step_heartbeat and composes it with the production OffsetCommit epoch fence, cross-checking every commit against an independent oracle of the expected epoch comparison and error code. It requires that no two members own one partition and that no member is advertised a partition another member still owns.

name: KIP-848 reconciliation model
bounds: The basic config has two members, two partitions, and epochs through 8; the wide config three members, two partitions, and epochs through 6.
outside: Offset commits, the offsets log, and the wire protocol remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production heartbeat step and the default uniform assignor over join, leave, and heartbeat actions with a faithful client that revokes before it adds and makes no cross-member check, so exclusivity must come from the coordinator's withholding alone. It requires that no two members own one partition at the same time and that no member is advertised a partition another member still owns.

name: Coordinator replay model
bounds: One group, two members, every group, member, assignment, topology, partition-metadata, and share-state record class, epochs -1, 0, 1, and i32::MAX, exact retries, mismatched value kinds, and every reachable log ordering through depth 16.
outside: Key parsing, schema decoding, transaction-marker interpretation, log reads, compaction, cache allocation, actor seeding, and process-crash atomicity remain host or I/O assumptions.
summary: Drives the production replay decisions shared by the consumer, share, and streams adapters. It requires key/value kind agreement, parent-before-child application, nonnegative monotonic epochs, assignment ownership by a present member, and whole-group tombstone dominance until a later group-metadata write, with witnesses for malformed type binding, orphan suppression, stale-epoch suppression, and i32::MAX.

name: Streams-group reconciliation model
bounds: Two member IDs, one subtopology with one or two tasks, three logical timeout ticks, topology epochs through two, group epochs through five, and one crash/replay in every reachable ordering.
outside: Request decoding, actor mailbox delivery, offsets-log append durability, cache publication, wall-clock scheduling, metadata-source snapshots, and internal-topic I/O remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production streams group membership, timeout, target-installation, and cooperative active-task transitions together with the port of Kafka's CurrentAssignmentBuilder and the replay adapters. A task pending revocation counts as still owned, so the properties require exclusive current and target active-task ownership, topology-valid assignments, nonnegative fenced epochs, coherent group phases, and exact durable replay projection.

name: EndTxn decision model
bounds: One transactional id with producer epochs up to 3 (basic, depth 11) and 6 (wide, depth 20).
outside: The KIP-360 identity classification and keepPreparedTxn recovery are not exercised.
summary: Runs one transactional id through every interleaving of an EndTxn split at its marker window, InitProducerId, AddPartitionsToTxn, and the completion task. It requires that an EndTxn whose Phase 3 finds the entry moved never writes Complete*, that each generation finalizes at most once, that InitProducerId never moves a Prepare* transaction, and that the epoch never regresses.

name: Exactly-once read composition model
bounds: Two transactional producers over one partition with one (basic, logs of 5 batches, depth 13) or two (wide, logs of 7 batches, depth 19) generations per producer.
summary: Runs two transactional producers and an advancing high watermark over one partition, driving the EndTxn cores and the production visibility window while modeling the LSO rule and the abort filter. Properties are checked against oracles derived by producer and control marker: the real window equals min(first unstable offset, hw), every committed record below it is visible, nothing above the HWM is visible, and no offset in an aborted range is visible.

name: KIP-939 timeout model
bounds: One transactional id, requested timeouts 1, 60000, 900000, 900001 and 0, a monotonic clock over 0, 1, 2, 60000, 60001, 900000, 900001, i32::MAX, i32::MAX + 1 and i64::MAX, and producer epochs up to 3 (basic, depth 20) and 5 (wide, depth 22).
summary: Runs InitProducerId with and without enable2Pc, AddPartitionsToTxn, EndTxn, completion, and the idle reaper over a clock that meets every timeout's start + timeout and start + timeout + 1. The headline property keys on the request's enable2Pc flag so a wrong encoding fails it, and the reaper properties compare every sweep with Kafka's timedOutTransactions rule in exact arithmetic.

name: Share-group membership model
bounds: Two member IDs, one topic with one or two partitions, four logical timeout ticks, epochs through five, and one crash/replay in every reachable ordering.
outside: Request decoding, actor mailbox delivery, offsets-log append durability, cache publication, wall-clock scheduling, metadata snapshot consistency, and share-state persister I/O remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production share group join, leave, and timeout transitions, the assignment reconciler and share assignor, the member-epoch fence, and the replay adapters. It requires unique (member, topic, partition) coordinates, bounded assignments for members at the target epoch, nonnegative fenced epochs, and exact durable replay projection; cross-member partition overlap remains intentional KIP-932 behavior when members outnumber partitions.

name: Share-partition state model
bounds: Two-member concurrency over three offsets with an in-flight limit of 3 or 1, plus failover with reload, deferral over the failover window, one-member deferral over three offsets, and log-start advance with reload.

pinned_states.config: two members, three offsets, in-flight limit 3
two members, three offsets, record lock limit 2

outside: The share-state persister, the fetch path, and wall-clock time remain outside the model.
summary: Holds the production KIP-932 acquisition state and drives it over every interleaving of consumer operations, time advance, KFC-1 deferral, a leader reload through the persisted batches, and a log-start advance. It requires a sorted, gap-free window covering exactly [start_offset, end_offset), exactly one owner for every acquired batch, lock bookkeeping matching the delivery state, a bounded delivery count, and a nondecreasing start offset.

name: Break-glass lifecycle model
bounds: One proposal over a small set of principals with a logical clock that expires it at 2 ms, in a two-of-three-approvers config and a three-of-four config.
outside: Signature verification, controller submission, and metadata durability remain outside the model.
summary: Drives one break-glass proposal through every interleaving of approve, withdraw, expire, and consume, building a real proposal record and calling the production approval and gate decisions against a real MetadataImage. It requires that no interleaving consumes the proposal twice, none consumes it with fewer than required_approvals distinct approvers, and a withdrawn proposal is never consumed.

name: Break-glass cross-spend model
bounds: Two open proposals in one MetadataImage under the same clock bound as the lifecycle model, in three configs: one action on two topics, a topic that looks like a partition of another, and two proposals that both cover one partition.
summary: Puts two open proposals in one image and runs every interleaving of approve, withdraw, expire, and consume against them. Each request carries a hand-written covered_by set taken from KFC-9's target-matching rule rather than from the broker's own covers, so the headline no_cross_spend property is not a tautology; removing the partition-target limit fails only the lookalike config and removing the consumed check fails all three.

name: Compaction model
bounds: Abstract logs of up to 4 entries (basic) and up to 5 entries (wide).
summary: Runs one pass of the cleaner over an abstract log per step, using the production key-indexing and retain decisions, and checks each pass's output against its input with rules computed from the two logs alone. The legacy cleaner, which indexes control keys and dedups markers by them, is run through the same checker and reports exactly control-not-deduped and marker-data-precedence as broken.

name: Leader-epoch reconciliation model
bounds: reconciliation_two_replicas has two replicas, epochs through 5, and three records per leader log; reconciliation_three_replicas has three replicas, epochs through 3, and two records; the regression config has two replicas, epochs through 4, and three records.
outside: Log start above 0, tiered storage, the below-log-start OFFSET_OUT_OF_RANGE, the follower's ListOffsets-based out-of-range recovery, wire encoding, and I/O remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production leader-epoch lookup on both sides of a fetch and the checkpoint truncation, with Kafka's LeaderEpochFileCache.assign, readRecords divergence gate, and fetcher truncation rules as the environment. It requires an accepted follower to be a prefix of the leader's log, no truncation to drop a shared record, every diverging_epoch to change the follower, and the leader never to answer OFFSET_OUT_OF_RANGE; a third config drops assign-at-election and must find the counterexample the assignment prevents.

name: KRaft model
bounds: three_voters_append checks three voters, one client append, leader epochs through two, at most two in-flight messages, and at most one crashed node at a time; other configs cover election safety, two-voter linearizability, message loss and duplication, and stateless appenders.
outside: Wire encoding, disk durability, wall-clock timing, volatile-state loss on restart, and behavior beyond the stated bounds remain outside the model.
summary: Runs the production quorum state machine for every node over an unordered network, with replication as the one abstracted exchange. It requires every node that believes it leads epoch e to hold each entry committed in an epoch at or below e, and its stale_candidate_refused witness requires a vote refused for log recency alone; removing the log-recency conjunct from handle_vote_request makes the config fail.

name: Throttle bucket model
bounds: bucket_basic checks two consumers, one reset between bursts 2 and 1, two clock units, and requests up to two; bucket_wide checks two consumers, two resets among (rate 1, burst 3), (2, 1), (0, 0) and (1, 0), two clock units, and requests up to two; bucket_fractional meters two storage units to a token and checks two consumers, one reset from (rate 1, burst 3) to (1, 1), two clock units, and requests up to two whole tokens.
outside: The clock is modeled in whole seconds with whole-token rates and memory as sequentially consistent; the part-token remainder is covered by unit tests.
summary: Drives the proved cap-and-grant arithmetic at every commit and steps the token bucket protocol one shared-memory access at a time. It requires available <= burst and exact token conservation per configuration, so a claimed refill can neither vanish nor be granted twice, and RED witnesses must find both bugs of the former lock-free seqlock design.

name: Audit spool model
bounds: Three record IDs, two loss events, a two-record spool, sync cadence two, and at most two crashes, in every reachable ordering.
outside: Filesystem and directory-sync semantics, storage hardware, sink durability, explicit operator recovery of poisoned replay, and behavior beyond the stated bounds remain outside the model.
summary: Drives the production spool append decision, the pending-loss helpers, the loss-batch settlement kernel, and the replay-recovery classifier, with a loss or a crash able to fall between any two of the writer's steps. It requires every durably admitted record to remain delivered or durably pending, at-most-once automatic delivery, exact loss accounting, distinct marker generations, and every durable marker settled exactly once.

name: Role succession model
bounds: Three candidates, a transaction coordinator that mints strictly increasing epochs, and a broker that rejects a write from a member whose epoch is not the newest minted one; a candidate can crash at any point.
summary: An exhaustive model of role succession that runs the production evaluate function itself rather than restating its rules: on every step it builds a role state from the model, asks evaluate what each member does, and applies that decision against a coordinator and a broker fence. A crashed candidate loses its producer session but keeps its registration until the coordinator expires it, so the model covers both a short pause that keeps the rank and a long outage that loses it.

name: Consumer lock-order model
bounds: The nine shared tokio::sync::Mutex fields of the classic Consumer and the lock-holding regions of the poll, seek, coordinator, and commit tasks, each cited by function and lock variable from the real source.
outside: The model abstracts away values such as offsets, partitions, and RPC payloads, and the network, keeping only which task holds which mutex and where each task is suspended.
summary: An exhaustive model of the classic consumer's async-Mutex lock protocol, built to settle whether the poll loop and the background coordinator task can deadlock through a lock-order cycle. Collecting every hold-one-while-acquiring-another edge from the real code gives an acyclic partial order, and the model proves the protocol deadlock-free across all task interleavings.

name: Producer client failover model
summary: An exhaustive model of producer-side failover routing at the client and server seam. It checks that stale metadata and a dead cached leader cannot make a prepared batch wedge forever: the batch either reaches the freshly elected leader quickly or fails within a bounded retry budget, and a retry preserves producer identity.
